endpoint.description: MCP_ENDPOINT -- the HTTP+JSON-RPC address of the MCP server this occupant bridges. It has NO default and that is the point (GH #489): unset means no server was named, and the cell then stays idle and answers every call with error_code=endpoint_unset instead of reconnecting to an address nobody chose. A guessed loopback default used to make every colony that grew this template carry a permanently failed cell after its first restart.

description.purpose: The bridge to one MCP server, as one occupant of this hive -- a cell, not a pattern: an MCP server is something a cell talks to, never something that stands in a colony.
description.use_when: NOT WIRED IN THE SHIPPED TREE and NAMING NO SERVER, and both halves are the configuration: no edge of this hive names this directory, and `MCP_ENDPOINT` has no default. Wiring it is a decision an operator makes after naming a server, in that order. Unwired is not on its own enough (GH #489): the derived inactivity of an island is a first-boot state that is not persisted, so a restart brings the occupant up. What makes that harmless is the empty endpoint -- with no server named the cell runs no handshake, stays idle and answers `endpoint_unset`.
description.not_in_scope: No server, no credential, no tool list of its own -- what an MCP server offers is what it answers, and this cell does not decide it. And no second name: this is `mcp` behind the tools door like every other occupant, reached on hop.tool_name, so an MCP tool is not a second kind of tool a caller has to know about.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result turn per call. hop.mcp_tool names the server-side tool -- and `__list_tools__` for the discovery round. NOTE: this cell stamps no `operation` and no `finish_reason`; a failure is `hop.error_code` and nothing else, which is why an exit edge for it must condition on `mcp_tool`. With no server named, every round -- discovery included -- comes back as `hop.error_code == 'endpoint_unset'` rather than as an empty answer.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: a tool_call turn whose text is the JSON arguments of the server-side tool.
examples: an operator names a server and draws the two edges -> the occupant wakes and serves hop.tool_name == 'mcp'

left as shipped -> nothing routes here (no edge names it), and if a restart brings it up anyway it holds no connection and calls nothing: `MCP_ENDPOINT` is unset, so any call it did receive comes back as error_code=endpoint_unset
